{{nihongo|'''Hiroomi Umezawa'''|梅沢 博臣|Umezawa Hiroomi}} (September 20, 1924 – March 24, 1995) was a [[physicist]] and [[Distinguished Professor]] in the Department of Physics at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]]<ref name="uwm-memorial-resolution">[http://www4.uwm.edu/secu/facdocs/2007.pdf Memorial resolution: Professor Hiroomi Umezawa], University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee Faculty Document no. 2007, September 21, 1995 (downloaded October 21, 2012)</ref> and later at the [[University of Alberta]]. He is known for his fundamental contributions to [[quantum field theory]] and for his work on [[quantum mind|quantum phenomena in relation to the mind]].

== Life ==
Umezawa obtained his PhD from [[Nagoya University]], [[Japan]] in 1952. He worked at the [[University of Tokyo]], Japan, and the [[University of Naples]], [[Italy]], and took up a position as professor at the [[University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee]] (UWM) in 1966, already considered a famous physicist at the time.<ref name="uwm-memorial-resolution"/> He joined the [[University of Alberta]], Canada, in 1975 when he took the Killam Memorial Chair as Professor of Physics, a position which he held until his retirement in 1992.<ref name="uwm-memorial-resolution"/><ref>[http://www.gradstudies.ualberta.ca/en/killam/chairs.aspx Killam Memorial Chairs] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202123650/http://www.gradstudies.ualberta.ca/en/killam/chairs.aspx |date=2014-02-02 }}, University of Alberta (downloaded 201 October 2012)</ref>

Umezawa is recognized as one of the eminent quantum field theorists of his generation.<ref name="uwm-memorial-resolution"/> He applied his results in quantum field theory also to [[high energy physics]], [[condensed matter physics]], [[nuclear physics]] and [[statistical physics]], as well as his considerations of quantum theory and the mind.<ref name="uwm-memorial-resolution"/>

== Quantum mind research ==
In 1967, together with L.M. Ricciardi, he proposed a quantum theory of the brain which posits a spatially distributed charge formation exhibiting spontaneous breakdowns at micro levels as the basis for processing at macro levels. In this model, the information resides in the virtual field associated with the dynamics of the cellular matter. This model was subsequently expanded by Stuart, Takahashi and Umezawa with their proposal of the development of long range correlations among neurons due to the interaction of two quantum fields. The approach was built upon by many others, including [[Karl H. Pribram]], and was later expanded by [[Giuseppe Vitiello]] to a [[Dissipative particle dynamics|dissipative]] quantum model of brain.<ref>{{Cite journal | doi=10.1142/S0217979295000380 | title=Dissipation and Memory Capacity in the Quantum Brain Model | year=1995 | last1=Vitiello | first1=Giuseppe | journal=International Journal of Modern Physics B | volume=09 | issue=8 | pages=973–989 | arxiv=quant-ph/9502006 | bibcode=1995IJMPB...9..973V | s2cid=14649535 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Vitiello |first=Giuseppe | doi=10.1075/aicr.32 | title=My Double Unveiled | series=Advances in Consciousness Research | year=2001 | volume=32 | isbn=978-90-272-5152-7 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | arxiv=q-bio/0309009 | last1=Pessa | first1=Eliano | last2=Vitiello | first2=Giuseppe | title=Quantum noise, entanglement and chaos in the quantum field theory of mind/Brain states | journal=Mind and Matter | year=2003 | volume=1 | page=59 | bibcode=2003q.bio.....9009P }}</ref>

== Memorial fund ==
After his death in 1995, Umezawa's family, friends and students set up the ''Umezawa Fund'' at the [[University of Alberta]] in his memory, dedicated to support studies in physics; among the ''Memorial Distinguished Visitors'' has been physicist [[Gordon Baym]] of the [[University of Illinois]] in 2007.<ref>Annual Report of the University of Physics Institute, University of Alberta, for the period of July 1, 2006 - December 31, 2008, published March 2010, [http://www.physics.ualberta.ca/Research/~/media/physics/Documents/Institutes/AR_2008_TPI.pdf#page=13 page 13] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116225159/http://www.physics.ualberta.ca/Research/~/media/physics/Documents/Institutes/AR_2008_TPI.pdf#page=13 |date=2013-01-16 }} (downloaded October 21, 2012)</ref>
